source_urls: https://scientificanglers.com/wp-json/wc/store/v1/products (WooCommerce Store API; descriptions contain the per-product spec tables)
how_the_lineup_is_organized: Scientific Anglers sorts its single-hand lines into price tiers and then reuses the same named tapers across them. Cheapest to priciest, the tiers are: Air Cel / Wet Cel ($30-60: basic floaters and sinkers, no slickness additive listed), Frequency ($60-70: AST slickness, welded loops, no SA Line ID), Mastery ($80-85: AST plus SA Line ID, the long-running core range), Amplitude Smooth ($99.95: AST Plus, which SA says gives 'up to five times less drag and eight times the durability of traditional lines'), Amplitude Textured ($129.95: the same AST Plus tapers with a Floating Texture tip and a Shooting Texture running line), and Magnitude Smooth or Textured ($149.95 / $179.95: clear-floating lines with a DuraCoat dual-polymer coating and EST+ additive; the freshwater Magnitude lines are 'optimized for use above 50F/10C'). Sonar is not a tier. It is SA's name for intermediate, sink-tip and full-sinking lines ($99.95), and Sonar Stillwater is its lake sub-family, built two line weights heavy with hang markers. Absolute is SA's leader and tippet brand (plus a flat mono shooting line), not a fly-line series. Taper names like MPX, Infinity, Trout GP, Trout Expert, Creek Trout, Anadro Indicator, Titan, Grand Slam and Bonefish describe the line's shape and job, and the same taper keeps the same numbers across tiers. For example, SA's tables list MPX WF5 with a 36 ft head, 175 gr head and 150 gr at 30 ft in Frequency, Mastery and Amplitude Smooth alike, and Infinity WF5 at 49 ft / 225 gr / 150 gr in Mastery, Amplitude and Magnitude. What you pay more for is coating, durability, slickness and texture, not a different taper. Each product page states how heavy the line runs (true to weight, quarter, half, three-quarter, one, one-and-a-half or two sizes heavy). In freshwater: Trout Expert (true to weight, long front taper) is the dry-fly line, Trout GP (quarter heavy) the general trout line, MPX (half heavy, the GPX successor) the all-rounder for fast rods and bigger flies, Infinity (half heavy, long head) the long-range mender, Creek Trout (one heavy, short head) the small-stream line, Anadro Indicator (1.5 heavy, long rear taper) the indicator-nymphing line, and Titan / Titan Long / Bass Bug (two heavy) the big-fly lines. Also match the line to water temperature: SA tags every line Cold/Medium or Hot. Tropical lines use Tropi-Core or a warm-weather coating, and a coldwater line goes limp in the heat. How to choose (our inference, not SA's wording): pick the taper for the job and the rod's speed, then the tier for budget. Smooth is quieter and easier on fingers and guides, while Textured shoots farther and floats higher but is noisier and costs $30 more.
